meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'sweet, piece of candy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here, I bought some sweets for the kids.

examples.trans: Here, I bought sweets for the kids. And the family is having a good time without me!

meanings.note: Уже месяц = for a month now. Common masculine noun meaning 'month' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('mint').

examples.trans: Do you want a mint candy?

examples.text: Мятную конфету к чаю не желаете?
examples.trans: Would you care for a mint candy with your tea?

examples.text: Луи украсил шоколадный десерт свежим мятным соусом.
examples.trans: Louis garnished the chocolate dessert with fresh mint sauce.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

meanings.note: Два года назад = two years ago. Core Russian adv meaning 'ago; back, backwards' in everyday speech.
Шаг назад = a step back. Core Russian adv meaning 'ago; back, backwards' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: To name or address someone. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call; to name', paired with 'назвать'.

To assign a title. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call; to name', paired with 'назвать'.

examples.trans: Call me simply Lev from now on.

examples.text: А вы называйте меня просто Вика.
examples.trans: And you call me simply Vika.

examples.text: Они называют себя лучшим рестораном города.
examples.trans: They call themselves the best restaurant in town.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: An inspection is underway at the bank.

examples.text: Эксперты уже начали проверку состояния старой стены.
examples.trans: Experts have already begun checking the condition of the old wall.

examples.trans: What needs to be done with this bird?

meanings.en: from above, on top, upstairs (соседи сверху = upstairs neighbours)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'верху').

examples.text: А он тут, соседи сверху бросили.
examples.trans: It's right here, the upstairs neighbours threw it.

examples.text: А он тут, соседи сверху бросили. Уже месяц висит на улице!
examples.trans: It's right here, the upstairs neighbours threw it. It's been hanging outside for a month already!

meanings.note: Дорожная служба = road service. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лужба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'service, department' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лужба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'service, department' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Дорожная служба обещала закатать её десять лет назад.
examples.trans: The road service promised to pave it over ten years ago.

meanings.note: Слышать о + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

Слышать о + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: Смотреть на + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

TV, a film. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трана'). Common feminine noun meaning 'country' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you!

examples.text: Над тобой вся страна смеётся! Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you! Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: 'ничего страшного'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трашный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible, scary').

'ничего страшного'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трашный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible, scary').

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.
